\section{Declarations}

\begin{theorem}[Monotonicity of neighbor averages]
\lean{Randomized.RegularMultigraph.avg_mono}
\label{Randomized.RegularMultigraph.avg_mono}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.RegularMultigraph.avg}
\difficulty{1}
Let $G$ be a finite regular multigraph of positive degree, and let $f,g:V\to\mathbb Q$.
If $f(v)\le g(v)$ for every vertex $v$, then at every vertex the average of $f$ over the
neighbors is at most the corresponding average of $g$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Average of a constant function]
\lean{Randomized.RegularMultigraph.avg_const}
\label{Randomized.RegularMultigraph.avg_const}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.RegularMultigraph.avg}
\difficulty{3}
Let $G$ be a finite regular multigraph of positive degree. The average of a constant
rational-valued function over the neighbors of any vertex equals that constant.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Zero miss probability at the target]
\lean{Randomized.RegularMultigraph.missProb_self}
\label{Randomized.RegularMultigraph.missProb_self}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.RegularMultigraph.hitProb_zero, Randomized.RegularMultigraph.missProb, Randomized.RegularMultigraph.missProb_succ}
\difficulty{4}
Let $G$ be a finite regular multigraph of degree $D>0$. For every vertex $t$ and every
nonnegative integer $k$, a length-$k$ sequence started at $t$ has miss probability $0$
for the target $t$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Initial miss probability away from the target]
\lean{Randomized.RegularMultigraph.missProb_zero_of_ne}

\end{theorem}

\lean{Randomized.RegularMultigraph.missProb_succ_le}

\begin{theorem}[Monotonicity of the miss probability]
\lean{Randomized.RegularMultigraph.missProb_antitone}
\label{Randomized.RegularMultigraph.missProb_antitone}

The probability that a length-$k$ sequence of uniformly chosen neighbor slots, started

\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Unreachable vertices have zero hit probability]
\lean{Randomized.RegularMultigraph.hitProb_eq_zero_of_not_reachable}
\label{Randomized.RegularMultigraph.hitProb_eq_zero_of_not_reachable}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.RegularMultigraph.Adj, Randomized.RegularMultigraph.hitProb, Randomized.RegularMultigraph.reflTransGen_of_hits, Randomized.idxProb}
\difficulty{3}
Let $G$ be a regular multigraph of degree $D>0$ on a finite vertex set, and let $s,t$ be
vertices. If there is no finite walk from $s$ to $t$, then for every natural number $k$,
the probability that a uniformly chosen sequence of $k$ neighbor indices starting at $s$
visits $t$ is zero.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Expected hitting time]
\lean{Randomized.RegularMultigraph.hitTime}
\statementsource{Vad12}{pdf-bf2ce5422088-p038-b006}
\label{Randomized.RegularMultigraph.hitTime}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.RegularMultigraph.missProb}
Let $G$ be a regular multigraph on a finite vertex type, with positive natural-number
degree $D$. For vertices $t$ and $s$ and a natural number $N$, the hit time from $s$ to
$t$ up to time $N$ is the sum of the miss probabilities at times $j=0,1,\varnothing,N-1$
for the walk on $G$ from $s$ relative to target $t$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Nonnegativity of truncated expected hitting time]
\lean{Randomized.RegularMultigraph.hitTime_nonneg}
\label{Randomized.RegularMultigraph.hitTime_nonneg}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.RegularMultigraph.hitTime, Randomized.RegularMultigraph.missProb_mem_Icc}
\difficulty{1}
Let $G$ be a finite $D$-regular multigraph with $D>0$, and let $t,s$ be vertices. For
each $j$, let $q_j(t,s)$ be the probability that a walk starting at $s$, choosing each
of its $j$ steps uniformly from the $D$ indexed neighbors, avoids $t$ at every visited
vertex, including its endpoint. For every integer $N\ge 0$, the sum
$\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}q_j(t,s)$ is nonnegative.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Hitting time from the target]
\lean{Randomized.RegularMultigraph.hitTime_self}
\label{Randomized.RegularMultigraph.hitTime_self}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.RegularMultigraph.hitTime, Randomized.RegularMultigraph.missProb_self}
\difficulty{1}
Let $G$ be a finite $D$-regular multigraph with $D>0$, and let $t$ be a vertex. For each
$j$, let $q_j(t,t)$ be the probability that a walk of $j$ steps starting at $t$,
choosing each step uniformly from the $D$ indexed neighbors, avoids $t$ at every visited
vertex, including its endpoint. For every integer $N\ge 0$,
$\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}q_j(t,t)=0$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Monotonicity of cumulative miss probability]
\lean{Randomized.RegularMultigraph.hitTime_le_succ}
\label{Randomized.RegularMultigraph.hitTime_le_succ}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.RegularMultigraph.hitTime, Randomized.RegularMultigraph.missProb_mem_Icc}
\difficulty{3}
Let $G$ be a finite regular multigraph of positive degree, and let $s,t$ be vertices.
For every natural number $N$, the cumulative miss probability for hitting $t$ from $s$
through step $N-1$ is at most the corresponding cumulative miss probability through step
$N$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Successive hitting-time identity]
\lean{Randomized.RegularMultigraph.hitTime_succ}
\label{Randomized.RegularMultigraph.hitTime_succ}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.RegularMultigraph.avg, Randomized.RegularMultigraph.hitTime, Randomized.RegularMultigraph.missProb_succ, Randomized.RegularMultigraph.missProb_zero_of_ne}
\difficulty{4}
Let $G$ be a finite $D$-regular multigraph with $D>0$, and let $s,t$ be distinct
vertices. For each $N\ge0$, let $H_N(t,v)$ be the sum, over $0\le j<N$, of the
probabilities that a uniformly chosen indexed-neighbor walk of length $j$ from $v$
avoids $t$ at every visited vertex, including its endpoint. Let $A H_N(t,s)$ be the
average of $H_N(t,\cdot)$ over the $D$ indexed neighbors of $s$. Then $H_{N+1}(t,s)=1+A
H_N(t,s)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Hitting time minus neighbor average]
\lean{Randomized.RegularMultigraph.hitTime_sub_avg_le}
\label{Randomized.RegularMultigraph.hitTime_sub_avg_le}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.RegularMultigraph.avg, Randomized.RegularMultigraph.hitTime, Randomized.RegularMultigraph.hitTime_le_succ, Randomized.RegularMultigraph.hitTime_succ}
\difficulty{2}
Let $G$ be a finite $D$-regular multigraph with $D>0$, and let $s,t$ be distinct
vertices. For each vertex $v$, define $H_N(t,v)$ as the sum, over $0\le j<N$, of the
probabilities that a uniformly chosen indexed-neighbor walk of length $j$ from $v$
avoids $t$ at every visited vertex, including its endpoint. Write $A
H_N(t,s)=\frac{1}{D}\sum_{i=0}^{D-1}H_N(t,G.\mathrm{nbr}(s,i))$ for the average of this
quantity over the indexed neighbors of $s$. Then $H_N(t,s)-A H_N(t,s)\le 1$ for every
integer $N\ge0$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Return time]
\lean{Randomized.RegularMultigraph.returnTime}
\label{Randomized.RegularMultigraph.returnTime}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.RegularMultigraph.avg, Randomized.RegularMultigraph.hitTime}
Let $G$ be a regular multigraph of degree $D$, with vertex $t$ and step bound $N$.
Define the return time at $t$ up to $N$ to be $1$ plus the average, starting from $t$,
of the hitting time of $t$ up to $N$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Upper bound for truncated return time]
\lean{Randomized.RegularMultigraph.returnTime_le_card}
\label{Randomized.RegularMultigraph.returnTime_le_card}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.RegularMultigraph.avg, Randomized.RegularMultigraph.hitTime, Randomized.RegularMultigraph.hitTime_self, Randomized.RegularMultigraph.hitTime_sub_avg_le, Randomized.RegularMultigraph.returnTime, Randomized.RegularMultigraph.sum_avg}
\difficulty{4}
Let $G$ be a finite regular multigraph of positive degree, and let $t$ be a vertex. For
every natural number $N$, the quantity obtained by adding $1$ to the average, over the
neighbors of $t$, of the sum of the miss probabilities at times $0$ through $N-1$ is at
most $|V|$, the number of vertices.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Squared differences and energy]
\lean{Randomized.RegularMultigraph.sum_sq_eq_energy}
\label{Randomized.RegularMultigraph.sum_sq_eq_energy}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.RegularMultigraph.avg, Randomized.RegularMultigraph.sum_swap}
\difficulty{4}
Let $G$ be a finite regular multigraph of positive degree $D$, and let $F$ be a
rational-valued function on its vertices. The sum, over all vertices and neighbor
indices, of the squared difference between $F$ at the vertex and at its indexed neighbor
is $2D$ times the sum over vertices of $F(u)$ multiplied by the difference between
$F(u)$ and its neighbor average.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Variation along a graph walk]
\lean{Randomized.RegularMultigraph.abs_sub_le_length_mul}
\label{Randomized.RegularMultigraph.abs_sub_le_length_mul}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.RegularMultigraph.Adj}
\difficulty{4}
Let $G$ be a regular multigraph of degree $D$, let $F$ assign a rational number to each
vertex, and let $a$ be rational. Suppose that for every vertex $x$ and every index $i$
among the $D$ neighbor indices, $|F(x)-F(G.\text{nbr}(x,i))|\le a$. For any vertex $t$
and any walk $p$ from $x$ to $t$ in the graph whose edges join adjacent vertices of $G$,
one has $|F(x)-F(t)|\le \operatorname{length}(p)\,a$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[A short graph walk]
\lean{Randomized.RegularMultigraph.exists_short_walk}
\label{Randomized.RegularMultigraph.exists_short_walk}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.RegularMultigraph.Adj}
\difficulty{4}
Let $G$ be a regular multigraph on a finite vertex set $V$, with positive degree. If
there is a finite sequence of neighbor steps from $x$ to $t$, then there is a walk from
$x$ to $t$ in the simple graph generated by the neighbor relation whose length is
strictly less than $|V|$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Energy bound on vertex values]
\lean{Randomized.RegularMultigraph.le_of_energy}
\label{Randomized.RegularMultigraph.le_of_energy}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.RegularMultigraph.Adj, Randomized.RegularMultigraph.abs_sub_le_length_mul, Randomized.RegularMultigraph.avg, Randomized.RegularMultigraph.exists_short_walk, Randomized.RegularMultigraph.sum_sq_eq_energy}
\difficulty{6}
Let $G$ be a finite regular multigraph of degree $D>0$, and let $F$ assign a rational
number to each vertex. Suppose $F$ is nonnegative everywhere, $F(t)=0$ at a vertex $t$,
and $F(u)-\operatorname{avg}_{v\sim u}F(v)\le 1$ whenever $u\ne t$, where the average is
over the $D$ neighbor slots of $u$. Suppose also that every vertex $u$ with $F(u)>0$ can
reach $t$ by a finite sequence of steps along those neighbor slots. Then, for every
vertex $u$, $F(u)\le 2D\,|V|^3$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Bound on cumulative miss probability]
\lean{Randomized.RegularMultigraph.hitTime_le}
\label{Randomized.RegularMultigraph.hitTime_le}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.RegularMultigraph.Adj, Randomized.RegularMultigraph.adj_symm, Randomized.RegularMultigraph.avg, Randomized.RegularMultigraph.hitTime, Randomized.RegularMultigraph.hitTime_nonneg, Randomized.RegularMultigraph.hitTime_self, Randomized.RegularMultigraph.hitTime_sub_avg_le, Randomized.RegularMultigraph.le_of_energy}
\difficulty{5}
Let $G$ be a finite regular multigraph of positive degree $D$, and let $s,t$ be vertices
such that $t$ is reachable from $s$ by a finite sequence of adjacency steps. For every
natural number $N$, the cumulative miss probability for hitting $t$ from $s$ through
step $N-1$ is at most $2D|V|^3$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Miss probability and cumulative miss probability]
\lean{Randomized.RegularMultigraph.succ_mul_missProb_le}
\label{Randomized.RegularMultigraph.succ_mul_missProb_le}
\leanok

\difficulty{3}
Let $G$ be a finite regular multigraph of positive degree, and let $s,t$ be vertices.
For every natural number $L$, $(L+1)$ times the probability of missing $t$ in a
uniformly chosen length-$L$ sequence of neighbor indices from $s$ is at most the sum of
the miss probabilities at times $0$ through $L$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Lower bound for hitting probability]
\lean{Randomized.RegularMultigraph.one_sub_le_hitProb}
\label{Randomized.RegularMultigraph.one_sub_le_hitProb}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.RegularMultigraph.Adj, Randomized.RegularMultigraph.hitProb, Randomized.RegularMultigraph.hitTime_le, Randomized.RegularMultigraph.missProb, Randomized.RegularMultigraph.succ_mul_missProb_le}
\difficulty{4}
Let $G$ be a finite regular multigraph of positive degree $D$, and let $s,t$ be vertices
such that there is a finite adjacency path from $s$ to $t$. For every natural number
$L$, the probability that a uniformly chosen sequence of $L$ neighbor indices visits
$t$, including at the starting vertex, is at least $1-2D|V|^3/(L+1)$, where $|V|$ is the
number of vertices.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Uniform hitting-time bound]

\begin{theorem}[Lower bound on the probability of hitting a target]

\begin{theorem}[Difference of truncated hitting times]
\lean{Randomized.RegularMultigraph.hitTime_sub_le}
\label{Randomized.RegularMultigraph.hitTime_sub_le}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.RegularMultigraph.avg, Randomized.RegularMultigraph.avg_mono, Randomized.RegularMultigraph.hitTime, Randomized.RegularMultigraph.hitTime_le_trunc, Randomized.RegularMultigraph.hitTime_nonneg, Randomized.RegularMultigraph.hitTime_self, Randomized.RegularMultigraph.hitTime_sub_avg_le, Randomized.RegularMultigraph.hitTime_succ, Randomized.RegularMultigraph.missProb, Randomized.RegularMultigraph.missProb_mem_Icc, Randomized.RegularMultigraph.missProb_self, Randomized.RegularMultigraph.missProb_succ, Randomized.RegularMultigraph.missProb_zero_of_ne}
\difficulty{5}
Let $G$ be a finite $D$-regular multigraph with $D>0$, and let $b,c,x$ be vertices. For
each target $t$ and starting vertex $v$, define $H_K(t,v)$ as the sum, over $0\le j<K$,
of the probabilities that a uniformly chosen indexed-neighbor walk of length $j$ from

\begin{theorem}[Hitting-time comparison through an intermediate vertex]
\lean{Randomized.RegularMultigraph.hitTime_le_add}
\label{Randomized.RegularMultigraph.hitTime_le_add}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.RegularMultigraph.hitTime, Randomized.RegularMultigraph.hitTime_sub_le, Randomized.RegularMultigraph.missProb, Randomized.RegularMultigraph.succ_mul_missProb_le}
\difficulty{5}
Let $G$ be a finite regular multigraph of positive degree, and let $a,b,c$ be vertices.
If there is a rational number $A$ such that, for every natural number $M$, the
cumulative miss probability for hitting $b$ from $a$ through step $M-1$ is at most $A$,
then for every natural number $N$ the cumulative miss probability for hitting $c$ from
$a$ through step $N-1$ is at most $A$ plus the cumulative miss probability for hitting
$c$ from $b$ through step $N-1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Miss probability after a cubic number of steps]
\lean{Randomized.RegularMultigraph.missProb_thousand_mul_pow_three_le}

\leanok
